text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Pulmonology consultation in two weeks with spirometry before and after bronchodilator, DLCO and FeNO, to confirm or refute asthma, separate it from COPD and heart disease, and plan treatment
  • Work-up of wheeze and breathlessness: chest X-ray, ECG, blood count with eosinophils, BNP, TSH and kidney function today; transthoracic echocardiogram before the consultation; albuterol continued as needed until testing, holding it for six hours before spirometry
  • Home blood pressure readings twice daily for a week, with a validated upper-arm cuff, because clinic readings are raised
  • Equity safeguards: spirometry read with race-neutral GLI Global equations, plain explanation of every result, and a check at each visit that her symptoms are not put down to her weight or age
  • GINA track 1: budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg as maintenance and reliever (one inhalation twice daily and one as needed, no more than 12 a day), albuterol stopped; inhaler technique, adherence and Asthma Control Test at every visit; a written asthma action plan with peak flow zones; review six weeks after any change and within a week of any exacerbation
  • Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: amlodipine 5 mg daily (a beta-blocker avoided because of asthma), a lower-salt diet, home readings, and kidney function and potassium at follow-up
  • Cardiovascular prevention: atorvastatin 20 mg daily for a 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent
  • Upper airway and reflux: fluticasone nasal spray and saline rinses, ear, nose and throat review with nasal endoscopy; omeprazole for eight weeks for heartburn with meal timing and head-of-bed elevation, then stop if settled
  • Weight and fitness, as she chooses: a dietitian visit, a walking plan she can follow on campus and in Washington, and a later discussion of medicines for weight if she wants one
  • Biologic assessment: not indicated while asthma is controlled on low-to-medium dose ICS-formoterol with good technique; repeat blood eosinophils and refer for biologic therapy if asthma becomes uncontrolled on step 4 to 5 treatment or there are two or more exacerbations needing oral corticosteroids in a year

resource.title: Mary McLeod Bethune synthetic care plan
resource.description: Confirm asthma in a 72-year-old Black woman with years of wheeze and breathlessness who has been treated with albuterol alone, and tell it apart from COPD and heart failure: spirometry with bronchodilator response interpreted with race-neutral equations, DLCO, FeNO and blood eosinophils, chest X-ray, BNP and echocardiography. Then treat on GINA 2025 track 1 (budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever, with SABA-only treatment stopped) and the 2020 NAEPP focused update, check inhaler technique and adherence before any step-up, write an asthma action plan, manage an exacerbation and review after it, assess for biologic therapy against the definition of severe asthma, and treat the comorbidities that worsen asthma (chronic rhinosinusitis, reflux, obesity without stigma) and the hypertensive heart disease found on the echocardiogram, with vaccinations; Black Americans have higher asthma death rates and race-based spirometry equations have hidden lung impairment, so each step is checked for under-treatment.
